newsitem.title: USA: Unimedia withdraws suit against Harmony.
newsitem.headline: Unimedia withdraws suit against Harmony.

text.p: France's SA Unimedia has withdrawn its pending lawsuit against Harmony Holdings Inc and sold some of its stock back to it, Harmony said Monday.

"The now settled and withdrawn lawsuit against (Harmony) arose out of a 1996 agreement between Unimedia and (Harmony) which, if completed, would have resulted in (Harmony's) acquisition of Unimedia," it said in a statement.
Unimedia sold back to Harmony 230,769 shares of Harmony common stock at $2.60 each, it said.
Harmony also said its chief executive officer, Harvey Bibicoff, sold to Children's Broadcasting Corp 600,000 of the 950,000 shares of common stock he owned and 550,000 of his 825,000 stock options.

"The purchase price for the shares was $2.50 per share and the purchase price for the options was $260,000 and 60,000 shares of CBC common stock," it quoted him as saying. "As part of the transaction, I signed a new, two-year employment contract."
Harmony said Bibicoff sold a portion of his stock position to the broadcasting company as part of a larger plan to affiliate Harmony with the company to benefit Harmony's long-term growth plan.

The Children's Broadcasting Corp also bought from Unimedia 769,231 shares of Harmony common stock at $2.60 a share, it said, adding that the company had consequently increased its ownership of Harmony to about 28 percent.
The company did not provide any more information and officials were not immediately available for comment.
Harmony Holdings produces television commercials, music videos, World Wide Web sites, and develops television programing and feature films.
Its stock was trading at 2-5/8 early Monday, down from a close of 2-23/32 on Friday.
